text:
Nora T: morning! on day 1 and i think my kubeconfig is weird. `kubectl config current-context` shows `redwood-dev`, but `kubectl get pods -n rl-infra` returns `Unauthorized` (401). i followed the onboarding steps. any quick checks?
Ben (DevEx): welcome Nora. can you paste the exact error and `kubectl config view --minify --raw` (redact tokens) and tell us if you're using okta or gcloud as your auth-provider?
Nora T: error: `You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)`. i'm using the Okta CLI flow (okta-aws or okta-kube?). i did `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` then `kubectl get ns` and got 401.
Alex P: common cause is an expired exec token in the kubeconfig or a leftover `user` entry. run `kubectl config view --raw | grep -A2 users -n` to see which user block is used. also `kubectl version --short` sometimes surfaces client exec errors.
Nora T: ran `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].user.exec.command}'` and it shows `okta-kube-helper`. i re-ran the okta login and it said login successful. still 401.
Ben (DevEx): two things to try: (1) check if your kubeconfig has `namespace: rl-infra` hard-coded under the context pointing to a team-SA; if so you might be impersonating a SA that hasn't been granted access yet. `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="redwood-dev")].context.namespace}'`
(2) check that your local kube cache isn't holding an expired token: `rm -rf ~/.kube/cache` then retry the okta exec.
Nora T: i checked, context namespace is empty. i removed `~/.kube/cache` and re-ran `kubectl get pods -n rl-infra` then got `Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces "rl-infra" is forbidden: User "nora@example.com" cannot get resource "namespaces" in API group ""` so now it's 403 not 401. progress? :sweat_smile:
Alex P: nice, 403 is progress. That means auth worked but RBAC denies you. New hires are not auto-added to `team-infra`; we map via the identity sync. Ben, can infra add a dev namespace or a scoped role?
Ben (DevEx): infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4901 to provision `nora-dev` and to check identity sync group membership. In the meantime, Alex, you can create a Role in `nora-dev` that grants read/list/watch on pods so she can run the tutorial.
Nora T: gracias. what caused the 401 initially? i want to avoid it for others.
Alex P: usually stale exec tokens or missing consent in Okta. Also if you accidentally merged another kubeconfig that points the context to a service account, you'll get 401 or 403 depending on token. Tip: `kubectl config get-contexts` shows the user; ensure it's your email user and not a SA.
Ben (DevEx): logging doc we link in onboarding covers this: re-run the exec login, clear `~/.kube/cache`, and verify identity sync status in the onboarding UI. i'll add a quick note to the doc about `~/.kube/cache` causing 401s.
Nora T: thanks all, will try stuff and ping if INFRA-4901 needs priority. excited to get the sample infra app running! :rocket:
